name: Sick young infant assessment (birth up to 2 months)
description: WHO IMNCI assess-and-classify for the sick young infant. A separate form from the 2-months-to-5-years assessment because the signs are different, not merely the thresholds: at this age serious illness is few-signed and non-specific, poor feeding alone means possible serious bacterial infection, and a low temperature is as ominous as a high one. Capture covers every input the young-infant classification tables evaluate.
sourceGuideline: WHO IMNCI — sick young infant age up to 2 months (engineering seed)

sections.title: Signs of possible serious bacterial infection
sections.description: Assess every one. At this age any single sign here means urgent referral, and the classification will not clear an infant whose signs were never looked for.

fields.label: Feeding
fields.description: Ask the mother and watch a feed. Poor feeding on its own is enough to classify possible serious bacterial infection.

fields.label: Convulsions
fields.description: Now or during this illness.

fields.label: Moves only when stimulated
fields.description: Watch the infant undisturbed first. Reduced movement is the young infant's equivalent of altered consciousness.

fields.label: Severe chest indrawing
fields.description: Deep and easily visible with the chest uncovered, in a calm infant.

fields.label: Temperature
fields.description: Both directions matter: 37.5 and above, or below 35.5.

fields.label: Respiratory rate
fields.description: Count for a full minute. The young-infant threshold is 60, not 40.

fields.label: Bulging fontanelle
fields.description: Assess with the infant calm and upright.

fields.label: Umbilicus
fields.description: Redness spreading to the abdominal skin is systemic; confined redness or pus is a local infection treated here.

fields.label: Skin pustules
fields.description: Many or severe pustules are treated as a systemic infection.

sections.title: Jaundice
sections.description: Three separate findings each make jaundice severe, for different reasons.

fields.label: Jaundice present
fields.description: Look at the skin and sclerae in daylight.

fields.label: Age in hours when jaundice appeared
fields.description: Onset within 24 hours of birth is always severe, whatever the depth of colour.

fields.label: Palms or soles yellow
fields.description: Yellow palms or soles means severe jaundice at any age.

fields.label: Diarrhoea
fields.description: Screens the dehydration table.

fields.label: Skin pinch
fields.description: Pinch the abdominal skin for one second and release.

sections.title: Feeding and weight
sections.description: A low weight for age in a young infant is a feeding problem until proven otherwise. The infant must be weighed: nothing can be dosed without a weight, and the classification will not clear an infant who was never weighed.

fields.label: Weight-for-age z-score
fields.description: Stamped by the growth registry at the time of measurement; shown here for the assessment.

fields.label: Attachment at the breast
fields.description: Observe a full feed rather than asking.

fields.label: Breastfeeds in 24 hours
fields.description: Fewer than eight is a feeding problem.

fields.label: Receives other foods or drinks
fields.description: Anything other than breast milk before six months.

fields.label: Oral thrush
fields.description: A common and treatable cause of poor feeding.

sections.title: Classification and plan
sections.description: The classification is a management category, not a diagnosis. Record any working diagnosis separately.

fields.label: Guideline classification
fields.description: As returned by the young-infant assess-and-classify tables.

fields.label: Working diagnosis
fields.description: Optional and separate. A classification groups conditions needing the same immediate action; recording it as a diagnosis would assert something no clinician stated.
